question: Does parameter-free Dual-Stream Mean Readout (DSMR) combined with Pair Update LayerNorm achieve the +10.4 meV gain observed with attentive pooling, or does effective dual-stream readout strictly require learned attention weighting?

hypothesis.observed_deficiency: The 100K DSAR result (+10.44 meV over baseline) conflated structural all-atom access with learned query-key attention gating. We do not know whether the virtual bottleneck is solved simply by averaging real atomic representations or whether dynamic chemical weighting across conjugated centers is indispensable.
alternative_explanations: Uniform mean pooling over real atoms dilutes localized orbital density with solvent/peripheral atom noise
Dynamic attention weights in DSAR were doing non-trivial selection of frontier orbital contributors
hypothesis.changed_mechanism: Parameter-free Dual-Stream Mean Readout combining [CLS] virtual token, virtual self-loop pair, and masked mean atom pooling over all non-padding nodes with Pair Update LayerNorm into a 544-dim readout head (5,312,353 parameters)
hypothesis.cheapest_falsifier: 60-epoch 100K/50K run failing to achieve 0.003 eV gain over the 0.156627 eV baseline (threshold < 0.153627 eV)
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_positive: adopt parameter-free Dual-Stream Mean Readout if it matches attentive readout, eliminating 33,025 gating parameters and reducing overfitting risk
hypothesis.decision_changed_if_negative: confirm that dynamic attention weighting is structurally required for dual-stream pooling and reject uniform mean pooling
